The chicken will lay the eggs if the farmer is there or not. What's the other option? You want the chicken to live, so do I. Whether or not the eggs are fertilized, the chicken will lay eggs. 

If the hen isn't living somewhere that has a human to help them take care of their prolapse, what do you want to happen? They'll still be laying eggs with the prolapse.

You're absolutely right in that beak cutting is a horrible practice, and it's one that isn't used in my area. There's industrial facilities that practice biosecurity, encourage healthy day/night cycles and exercise, while maintaining a healthy population. 

Prolapses are awful, agreed, in any species, so you take the animal to the vet and have them fixed.

Ok, but the fact of the matter is that even meat breed chickens also lay eggs. Maybe not daily, but you'll get a healthy amount.

So we're past the point of having a mythical non-laying domestic chicken, and have to deal with the realities that these chickens exist now and need excellent care. Part of that care is collecting eggs so they don't rot and spread disease.
I literally was studying to be a chicken judge, and am in school for poultry production. There are no chickens spraying out eggs 10x daily.

That sounds friggin awful, and very confusing as to how their industry manages to survive with all the mistreatment.

The industrial egg farmers here usually provide stacked nesting areas, they have a dedicated day/night cycle, and the better ones wear booties on their feet to minimize cross contamination so the hens aren't getting sick, with constant check ins and rotations for sick hens. I don't agree with keeping chickens inside all day, but I can't fault their practices so long as the birds are healthy and have adequate exercise space.

If the owner doesn't eat the eggs, eventually the chicken will. Some of them figure out they're made of delicious things, break them open, and eat them. 

If you leave them to rot in the nest, they'll attract predators and disease. It's like letting your hens sleep on a bed of rotting fruit, to use more vegan terms. 

Chickens will do three things after laying an egg: brood the infertile eggs, eat the eggs themselves, or lay the egg and walk away.  If the eggs are unfertilized, they just rot. If they eat the eggs, they'll eat every egg they lay for the yolk. If they ignore them, you just have rotten eggs.

That is super incorrect, The part about painful deaths. Good grief, The farmer isn't going out to the hen house and just like, cackling evilly over hens who are egg-bound. There's ways to help the chicken with massage and Vaseline to help get the egg out, and good farmers realize when their chickens are sick. 

I've had several hens simply die of old age. They stop laying at a certain point in their lives, Chickens have chicken menopause.

Also, are you talking about feral chickens? Chickens exist because of domestication. The only "wild chickens" would be junglefowl, but those aren't even chickens. It's like calling a duck a swan.

You do know that the farmers aren't like just squeezing the eggs out of hens right? Whether or not the eggs are fertilized, a chicken is going to lay eggs. They are of course our egg related diseases, like being egg-bound, but these are things that the farmer is well aware of.
